newsitem.title: USA: Ameritech to open European office Oct. 24.
newsitem.headline: Ameritech to open European office Oct. 24.

text.p: Ameritech Corp said Friday it will open an office in Brussels on October 24 as part of its plan to continue to expand services in Europe.

"It's a continuation of a strategy we started just a few years ago," Richard Notebaert, chairman and chief executive of Ameritech, said in an interview. "Brussels is the center of Europe...it has always been a crossroads of Europe."
Notebaert said Ameritech has invested a total of more than $2 billion in Europe. The company has interests in most European countries, including Poland and Hungary in Eastern Europe.
The new office will have a permanent staff of about a dozen, he said.

With the opening of the new office, the company expects to add services, Notebaert said. He declined to give specific plans, but said the company has extensive opportunities in electronic commerce, entertainment, long distance telephone service and security.
In second quarter more than 20 percent of Ameritech's earnings came from international investments, Notebaert said.
"It's very healthy," he said of the international operations.
Notebaert said he expects Ameritech's investments in Belgium and Hungary to be especially profitable.
"I think (they) will be in the category of what we've done in New Zealand as far as the value to shareholders," Notebaert said.

He said the company initially invested about $1.2 billion in Telecom Corp of New Zealand in 1990. It got $1.2 billion back after dividends and selling half of its position, and still owns a 24 percent stake now valued at about $2 billion.
